highlights.title: Video game ownership bill introduced in Congress
highlights.summary: Rep. Ritchie Torres of New York's 15th congressional district in the Bronx introduced the Power To The Players Act this week. If passed, the bill would direct the Federal Trade Commission to establish regulations that guarantee consumers ownership of a game when they pay for it, rather than a…
body: The Power To The Players Act would guarantee buying a game means you own it, not license it.

It’s increasingly common for games sold to require a connection to a server. Meaning that when a company decides to shut down those servers, the games often become unplayable. Rep. Torres singles out NBA 2K25 as a recent example. 2K will be delisting the game from storefronts at the end of the month and shutting down its servers on December 31st, limiting its playability.

Concerns around ownership, the ability to play, resell, or transfer games have drawn attention recently following Sony’s announcement that it planned to phase out physical game discs in 2028. In a statement announcing the bill, Rep. Torres said, “A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale.”

highlights.title: Arsenal win with one shot on target as Forest sink into bottom three
highlights.summary: Arsenal's only shot on target proved enough to snatch victory at Nottingham Forest through Noni Madueke's deflected strike, keeping the champions within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City and condemning Forest to the relegation zone.
body: After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. Murillo almost salvaged a point in stoppage time with a superb solo run, driving at the Arsenal defence before curling narrowly wide. Ezri Konsa then made a crucial late challenge to deny Liam Delap.
However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.

highlights.title: 36 Years Later, Robert De Niro's Greatest Gangster Movie Quote Is Still One of a Kind
highlights.summary: Few actors have done more to shape the modern cinematic gangster than Robert De Niro. Across decades of mob dramas, he's played men who command respect through intimidation, calculation, and a religious devotion to the rules of their world.
body: Through all these roles, De Niro has delivered plenty of unforgettable lines, but one of his most memorable isn't a threat or a declaration of power. It's a deceptively simple piece of advice, one that succinctly sums up the gangster mentality built on loyalty. Ripped from Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas (based on Nicholas Pilegg's non-fiction crime chronicle Wiseguy ), De Niro’s James “Jimmy” Conway offers the following sage advice: "Never rat on your friends and always keep your mouth shut."

The line comes after a young Henry Hill (Ray Liotta) refuses to talk following a bust for selling untaxed cigarettes, earning his stripes by making it through his first court appearance without informing on any of his accomplices. Outside the courtroom, Conway slips him a handful of cash and congratulates him on surviving his first pinch. Then he pulls Henry close and imparts the cardinal rules of their world, turning a low-level arrest into a defining rite of passage for a kid desperate to prove his place in the organization.
points: Few actors have done more to shape the modern cinematic gangster than Robert De Niro.
Across decades of mob dramas, he's played men who command respect through intimidation, calculation, and a religious devotion to the rules of their world.

highlights.title: Taylor Swift Fires Up Academy Gala With Four Songs in Her First Band Performance Since the Eras Tour
highlights.summary: Taylor Swift got some of the old gang back together for her first full-band performance since the Eras Tour, delivering a four-song set to a black-tie audience Saturday night at the Academy Museum 6th Annual Gala.
body: As expected, she also sang her contender for the 2027 Oscars, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from the Pixar film “Toy Story 5.” It wasn’t her first live performance ever of that song — she did it at the Grammy Museum and at a private Ross House FYC showcase — but it was her first time singing it live with a full band, and not as part of a mash-up. Besides its Oscar eligibility, the song is also in contention at the Grammys, entered in the song of the year category as well as film soundtrack and country divisions.
For the remaining two slots in her set, Swift dug farther back into the past, covering both her cynical and romantic bases, opening with “Blank Space” and ending with “Love Story.”
Wearing a Ralph Lauren gown for her performance, Swift invited the formally clad gathering to dance along with her set, saying, “Dancing is absolutely allowed. It’s not mandatory, but it’s more fun.”

highlights.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
highlights.summary: Anthropic has granted external evaluators “employee-like access” to assess the risks of its models, following through on a commitment to increase safeguards over concerns the technology could run catastrophically out of control.
body: METR, a nonprofit that has worked with leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office with access to its hardware and internal systems.

A greater role for third-party evaluators is among the main concrete steps the labs have proposed in response to rising concern about the dangers more capable AI systems could pose to the economy, cyber security and humanity at large.

Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei achieved a rare moment of unity with arch-rivals Sam Altman and Elon Musk in September when the OpenAI and SpaceX bosses rallied behind his proposal to embed external auditors in the leading labs.
Thursday’s announcement marks the first step to implementing these pledges. OpenAI has yet to lay out plans to bring in evaluators after Altman said Amodei’s proposals were a good idea.

highlights.title: Giving AI a “crystal clear” view of the materials world
highlights.summary: New research can help AI models understand crystalline materials in 3D and reason about their properties.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."

In principle, artificial intelligence could make finding the right material for an application as simple as ordering dinner: Scientists would tell a large language model what they want, and it would serve them a perfectly designed crystal for the job.

Unfortunately, that approach doesn’t work well yet, and the problem comes down to data: Most materials consist of crystals, which are 3D periodic arrangements of atoms whose structures are stored in specialized formats, not the text streams that today’s large language models are trained on. The experimental literature is also heavily biased toward a few popular classes of crystals, making AI outputs skew toward those materials.

And a game that concluded with another dose of boot-fuelled drama following Cam Little's last-second winner against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham the previous week.
Texans quarterback CJ Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns while Jaylin Noel led his side with four receptions for 107 yards and a score as Houston improved to 2-4 on the year.

Stroud's first interception of the season came by way of Travis Hunter as the two-way Jags star became the first player to score a touchdown and record a pick in the same game since Brian Dawkins for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Texans on September 29, 2002.
Trevor Lawrence finished 24 of 41 for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception as the Jaguars slipped to 4-2 at the end of their fortnight in the UK.

highlights.title: Battlefield 6 devs to fix "Secuty" skin typo, but five-pistol outfit was intentional
highlights.summary: Battlefield Studios has responded after fans accused it of using AI to generate cosmetics after spotting a "Secuty" typo on a Battlefield 6 Season 5 skin.
body: The studio acknowledged "candid feedback" from players in a statement on social media, insisting it had "hear[d] your concerns".

And though the statement did not mention AI - either to admit or deny using the generative tech - BattlefieldComm said that while the 'Secuty' typo will be addressed by a "correction update", an outfit with five pistols is intentional.

"First, let's dive into the 'Secuty' typo patches on the McNeil character," the studio wrote. "A correction update has already been planned for the Season 5 Phase 2 release. However, we recognise that letting a known visual error go live without quick acknowledgement creates confusion and erodes trust. We are reviewing how we communicate known visual bugs so you aren’t left wondering whether something was intentional or overlooked."

The five-pistol-touting Midnight Mirage skin, however, is described as an "intentional creative concept" and "a nod to over-the-top action movie tropes where an operative inexplicably has another backup weapon strapped to every spare inch of gear".

highlights.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.title: There are five signs that someone dislikes you – but it’s best to ignore them | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: All the possible indications, from eye contact to body language, come with a disclaimer. The truth is, you can never be totally sure... I’d be far less paranoid if everyone wasn’t out to get me, so when BBC Science Focus dangled “ The subtle signs somebody secretly dislikes you ”, I’ve never…
body: The first indication? They avoid eye contact. Apparently “someone who repeatedly looks away, scans the room or avoids mutual gaze might be creating psychological distance”. Agreed. But they may also be checking to see who else arrives, which might not mean they secretly hate you, only that they secretly don’t like you as much as whoever just came in.

The second sign is unarguably more convincing. “Their facial expressions show contempt or disgust.” Admittedly, I’m no psychologist, but still, if someone looked contemptuous or disgusted while interacting with me, I’d be pretty confident in concluding that they aren’t my greatest fan all on my own. File this one under bear/woods, pope/Catholic.

Third up, they “smile less around you”. This feels dangerous, because the only way to know whether they are smiling less around you than other humans they come into contact with is to put them under surveillance and keep a tally. If they didn’t dislike you before you hid in a bush counting their grins, they probably would afterwards.

highlights.title: Man Utd held by Leeds as winless run continues
highlights.summary: Manchester United delivered a more committed performance in a changed formation but were held to a 1-1 draw by Leeds as pressure on Michael Carrick continues to grow.
body: In a week that included defeat to Atletico Madrid and an explosive interview from Lisandro Martinez - who started at Elland Road - the noise was calmed somewhat by a display that showed character, if not enough quality to claim a second league win of the season.
United played without a recognised striker for the majority, allowing Youri Tielemans a more offensive role and he combined with Bryan Mbeumo to open the scoring in the first half.
But Carrick's side faded badly as the game went on, another fixture in which they were outrun, eventually pegged back by an instinctive Dominic Calvert-Lewin strike from a poorly defended corner.

Leeds away was pitched as the worst game to end a fractious week. In reality, it forced United to scrap and that at least appeared to show appetite for the fight. "In isolation, going to Leeds and performing how they did was a decent result," reflected Jamie Carragher. They were helped by the fact that Daniel Farke's side were not at their battling best either.

highlights.title: The kindness of strangers: After my wife died, a football club made an extraordinary gesture
highlights.summary: My son had only played two seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough, five years earlier. I don’t know how they even got our new address but they took the time to send him a care package. Footy clubs, and the AFL specifically, have a lot to answer for in terms of sexism.
body: When we lived in Melbourne many years ago, my son played a couple of seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough. Unfortunately for him, I secured a job in central Queensland and moved the family north.

During our new adventure, my wife was diagnosed with breast cancer. It was stage four, so she was in trouble straight away. She battled it fiercely but died in 2015, about five years after we left Melbourne.

As my children and I began to emerge from the fog of grief, a package arrived in the mail for my son. Inside was a St Mary’s Greensborough football jersey with our surname emblazoned across the back. Attached was a note that read: “Thinking of you after the loss of your mum.”
The support around us as a family when my wife was sick, and when she died, was fantastic. I am so grateful for that. But sometimes it’s the gestures that come out of left field that really move you.
points: My son had only played two seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough, five years earlier.

highlights.summary: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page: … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages…
body: Language that experts say allowed the scraping of news sites to train its AI has been removed from Meta’s terms.

Many, including Neiman Lab and James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, interpreted it as an attempt to give Meta the right to use content scraped from sites to train its AI products for free and supersede blocking instructions in a site’s robots.txt file.

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers. As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”

highlights.title: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
highlights.summary: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years ago. A few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about.
body: You could say that I fell down a Wiki rabbit hole, especially when it came to the website’s early years. Almost everything important about the project came together quite quickly. Its amateurish, homegrown ethos was off-putting to a lot of writers and journalists, and that meant many questions about why it had worked had no answers. Most of the people seriously interested in Wikipedia were a handful of academics – so I decided to write a book about it.

Because Wikipedia is so massive, writing an “exhaustive” book on it is impossible, like trying to represent a mountain with a grain of sand. Instead, I concentrated on the human history – the small, sometimes very small, number of people who really influenced what Wikipedia became. Wikipedians can be difficult, and the most ornery get a bad wrap – even the Wikimedia Foundation’s leadership has made comments about their “Dorito-stained fingers”, or tendency to stay home on a Saturday night. But by the end of the process, I was in awe of them, and I still am.

highlights.title: 8 Mass Effect Replay Ideas That Make the Trilogy Feel Brand-New
highlights.summary: Every replay of the Mass Effect games tends to start with a promise: this time, you’ll do things differently. Then Shepard makes the same speech, you bring the same squad, and you’re right back where you started.
body: The Renegade path is an uneven one in this trilogy. Your dialogue options are color-coded: You get a blue, diplomatic Paragon option and a red, ruthless Renegade one. The red options mean different things at different times. In Mass Effect 1, they swing between prejudice, efficiency, and plain rudeness. By the time you get to Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3, the Renegade options settle on one primary idea: Getting the job done at any cost. One effective approach, is to take the red option nearly every time, and go Paragon only for the choices the sequels depend upon. Be ruthless, but leave a few people alive. Like Wrex, at least. For the story’s sake.

Mass Effect 1 asks you to pick a pre-service history (Spacer, Colonist, or Earthborn) and a psychological profile (Sole Survivor, War Hero, or Ruthless). Each history and profile unlocks its own mission, like “Old Friends” for Earthborn Shepards, where a former gang member asks you for a favor.

highlights.title: Forget the seven-year itch: opposite-sex marriages more likely to end after two decades
highlights.summary: ONS data for England and Wales shows 26% of heterosexual divorces in 2025 followed 20 years or more of marriage. Most couples are aware of the dreaded “seven-year itch”, when the honeymoon period wears off and real life starts to bite.
body: Now official data has shown that couples in England and Wales are more likely to split after 20 years. According to Office for National Statistics figures, more than a quarter of all divorces between opposite-sex couples happened after 20 years or longer of marriage.

The former Strictly presenter Tess Daly recently separated from her husband, the presenter Vernon Kay, after 22 years of marriage. The Downton Abbey actor Hugh Bonneville split from his wife, Lulu Williams, in 2023 after 25 years, and in 2019, Colin Firth announced his separation from wife, Livia Giuggioli, after 22. Last year, the Hollywood actor Nicole Kidman and singer Keith Urban separated after almost 20 years of marriage.

Divorce lawyers have previously said some couples are putting off splitting up because of the cost of living crisis. Recent figures have shown the average length of a marriage ending in divorce in England and Wales reached a record high last year.

ONS figures have long appeared to show that the seven-year itch exists; since records began in 1963, the largest proportion of divorces each year has almost always been among those who have spent between five and nine years as a couple.

highlights.title: J Mascis has nothing better to do
highlights.summary: Dinosaur Jr. frontman J Mascis is known as something of a slacker guitar god. He stands stoically onstage, barely moving, as he seemingly effortlessly works through deft guitar solos and lopsided riffs.
body: That’s not to say that Mascis can’t be funny or charming. As our interview was winding down and I was thanking him for his time, he started to loosen up a bit. He told me about his youth as a mini golf “enthusiast.” “I had a 3-foot putt for the win” at a mini-golf tournament, he said, but “that’s when I realized that I was a choker … When I was 11, I choked.” And that’s when he decided, “I should maybe not do sports.” So, instead of becoming a professional mini golfer, Mascis went on to form one of the most important bands in alternative rock.

While most of his contemporaries have called it quits or are just going through the motions onstage for a paycheck, the original lineup of Mascis, bassist Lou Barlow, and drummer Patrick Murphy are still regularly putting out new LPs of reliable rockers. But Mascis says there isn’t any grand secret to the band’s longevity. Over 40 years deep, he says, “I guess we have nothing better to do.”

What, for an interviewer, can come off as frustrating indifference might actually be the key to Mascis’ staying power — for better or worse. Creatively and professionally, his modus operandi seems to be rolling with the punches and not overthinking things.

But, for the fifth time under Glasner in all competitions, there was not a goal to celebrate in front of the club’s home fans.

It was a game that came to feel increasingly set up for the famous terrace chant. One-nil to the Ars-en-nal. Or, as the travelling hordes would have it, one-nil to the champions. Arsenal did not play well. They created little, finishing with just one shot of target. How Noni Madueke made it count.

On as a half-time substitute, the winger took a pass from Declan Rice in the 80th minute and had only one thing on his mind. To cut inside from the left and unload. The connection was pure and that was when he caught a break, which he has worked to earn after a difficult start to the season. The ball deflected off Jair Cunha and flew past the Forest goalkeeper, Matz Sels.

highlights.title: Great Pottery Throw Down judge Keith Brymer Jones looks back: ‘Men like seeing me be emotional’
highlights.summary: The potter and presenter on a tricky childhood, his religious calling for clay, and cross-dressing as Adele. Born in London in 1965, Keith Brymer Jones is a potter, ceramic designer and TV judge.
body: This photo was taken in our family home in Finchley. Socks, shorts and a T-shirt was my usual outfit for scabbing around in the garden aged 11. I was a complete and utter square.

My main passion at this time was dancing – ballet, tap and Highland and Scottish country dancing. But I was starting to realise I should stop telling people about it. I was about to embark on my first year of secondary school at St Mary’s in Hendon and knew I’d get stick for it.

I kept it under wraps, but I was bullied for three years. It was the start of a difficult part of my life, especially after my grandfather died. His death happened in front of me, when he fell down the stairs while having a heart attack. Unsurprisingly, my OCD developed around this time; I used it to try to create a sense of control and order. Everything around me had to be at 90 degrees – pens, pencils and the curtains. My bedroom began to resemble an empty studio, because it was easier than having belongings. To this day, I do like a tidy workshop.

highlights.title: What are self-replicating ‘AI worms’, and why is Anthropic worried about them?
highlights.summary: The tech company says successful AI worms need more capability on less powerful devices, but current trends make that feasible by the end of the year. Warnings about what artificial intelligence might do in the future – together with alarming reports of what it has gotten up to already – are being…
body: Yet a report this week from Anthropic’s offensive research team grabbed attention by describing a new, practical threat, one devoid of human characteristics or apocalyptic musings. The red team, as such internal testers are called, said it created a malicious AI program that spread autonomously through internet-connected “smart” televisions and could do the same inside other ordinary devices. While machines running AI usually need a fair amount of computing power, the researchers said that their program split parts of itself among 15 televisions and was still able to function by using a bit of power from each.

In addition to evoking the horcruxes that kept pieces of Lord Voldemort’s soul alive within objects in the Harry Potter series, the report alarmed some professionals because the generally weak security of smart televisions and many other “internet of things” devices would be very hard to correct, even with a concerted effort.

highlights.title: Street Fighter Fails To Match Resident Evil's Opening Weekend Box Office Success
highlights.summary: Looking at the fall slate of blockbuster films, I was most interested in finding out whether Resident Evil or Street Fighter would have the bigger opening weekend. We now have our answer: Street Fighter grossed about half of what Resident Evil did in its first weekend.
body: Deadline reports that Street Fighter, an adaptation of Capcom's series of fighting games, grossed $31 million its opening weekend. By comparison, the Capcom horror game adaptation Resident Evil made $60 million its opening weekend and is still charting at the box office about a month after release.

Street Fighter is opening lower than Mortal Kombat 2, another fighting game adaptation released this year, and doing worse than what you'd expect from a blockbuster movie. Ultimately, its gross ended up in line with industry pre-release expectations, though. The real overperformer of the weekend was the Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything, which had the second-biggest opening for a theatrically released documentary ever at $15 million.

Street Fighter and Resident Evil took two very different approaches to adaptations. Street Fighter leaned into well-known characters, fan service, and the wackiness of the IP to draw people in. Meanwhile, Resident Evil took the essence and themes of its franchise and used them to tell a completely original story.

highlights.title: Betty McGuire, Actress on Broadway and ‘Growing Pains,’ Dies at 100
highlights.summary: She worked alongside Ethel Merman, Bea Arthur and Susan Hayward on the stage, was Joanna Kerns’ mom on the ABC sitcom and played a nun in ‘Up in Smoke.’
body: Betty McGuire, who appeared three times on Broadway and recurred as the mother of Joanna Kerns’ Maggie Seaver on the ABC sitcom Growing Pains, has died. She was 100.

McGuire died Oct. 8 of natural causes at the Motion Picture & Television Country House and Hospital in Woodland Hills, close family friend Keith Gerchak, an actor and co-founder of Double G Films, told The Hollywood Reporter.
In 1978 films, she portrayed Sister Mary Quacker in Cheech & Chong’s Up in Smoke and a nurse in the Michael Crichton medical thriller Coma, starring Geneviève Bujold.

Born on March 20, 1926, in Bridgeport, Connecticut, McGuire performed and understudied on Broadway alongside the likes of Ethel Merman, Barbara Cook, Bea Arthur and Tony Randall in the original productions of the musicals Plain and Fancy in 1955-56, Happy Hunting in 1956-57 and Oh, Captain! in 1958.

body: The guys also react to Missouri-Ole Miss, Kentucky-Oklahoma, Houston-Oklahoma State, Wisconsin-UCLA, Mississippi State-LSU, Penn State-Michigan, Nebraska-Oregon, Rutgers-Maryland, Northwestern-Michigan State and plenty more from one of the wildest days in recent memory.
And of course, Steve will give a full breakdown of his time in Provo.
